subject: URGENT: 429 spikes and timeouts affecting HealthRails production
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@healthrails.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@healthrails.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: 429 spikes + timeouts — urgent

Monica —

We started seeing a significant spike in 429 responses and timeouts hitting our production endpoints around 07:50 PDT. Error rate jumped to ~18% for token gen calls and several of our background workers are entering retry loops, which pushed end-to-end latencies from ~220ms to >2s for user-facing flows. We have customers experiencing UI failures right now.

Attached is a short sample of the errors we see (healthrails_error_sample_20270721.log). Key points:
- 429 bursts concentrated on a subset of projects (project IDs included in the log)
- Retries appear aggressive from our side (backoff configured), but status codes are immediate 429, not transient 503
- No config changes on our side in the last 24h

Can your team triage immediately and confirm whether this is quota/rate-limit behaviour from Redwood or something on our routing? We can join a bridge. This is blocking important customer sessions.

— Evan
Evan Cole
Head of Platform, HealthRails
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@healthrails.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@healthrails.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 429 spikes + timeouts — urgent

Evan — thanks for the alert and the log sample. We’re escalating to infra immediately.

Short plan:
1) I’ve opened a priority incident and asked infra to verify quota assignment and routing for the affected org/projects (INF-8421).
2) Can you share the HubSpot project IDs + any non-prod project IDs you suspect? That will help us map quickly.
3) We’ll stand a bridge in 15 minutes and push a short-lived rate uplift if we confirm org-level misassignment.

Rishi / Naomi — I’ve looped you. Rishi, please start with quota mapping snapshot + rolling back any recent tiering changes to this tenant if that’s where the problem is. Naomi, please prepare comms for HealthRails execs (short impact summary + ask).

I’m attaching the error sample you sent into the incident.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | monica.patel@redwood.ai
(attachment: healthrails_error_sample_20270721.log)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: 429 spikes + timeouts — urgent

On Wed, Jul 21, 2027 at 8:12 AM Evan Cole <evan.cole@healthrails.com> wrote:
> Monica —
> We started seeing a significant spike in 429 responses...

I pulled the quota-mapping snapshot for HealthRails org and there is a mis-assignment on the org->project tier mapping. A change deployed at 02:37 UTC this morning (internal rollout) inadvertently swapped the tier alias used for a subset of HealthRails projects, assigning them to a lower-rate pool than intended. That explains the concentrated 429s.

Immediate remediation I recommend (short horizon):
- Apply a temporary project-level uplift (2x token throughput) for the affected project IDs (we can do this within 10 minutes).
- Put a request-side circuit breaker in routing so retries from HealthRails reduce aggressive replays for 30m.
- Revert the alias swap in the tiering service to restore original mapping; we’ll roll revert today behind a canary.

Longer term: add a validation gate in the alias rollout that prevents ambiguous alias collisions across org tenants and a preflight dry-run that verifies per-project capacity against SLOs.

I’m attaching the quota-mapping snapshot for the affected projects (quota-mapping-snapshot-20270721.json).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: quota-mapping-snapshot-20270721.json)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Evan Cole <evan.cole@healthrails.com>, Priya Menon <p.menon@healthrails.com>, Jake Soto <jsoto@healthrails.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: HealthRails 429 spike — ask for temporary uplift + credits

Team —

Quick executive brief for leadership: HealthRails (HLR-2987) is experiencing a production-impacting 429 spike caused by an alias/tiering misassignment during this morning’s rollout. Impact: 
- ~18% 429 rate on user-facing gen calls between 07:50–08:10 PDT
- Increased tail latency, several customer sessions failed; potential revenue-impacting support tickets in flight
- Retry storms on their side increased token consumption and cost exposure for both sides

Requesting leadership sign-off for the following immediate actions:
1) Approve an emergency project-level throughput uplift for the affected HealthRails projects for 60 minutes to stabilize user traffic.
2) Approve a one-off partial credit for excess token consumption during the incident window (we’ll quantify but expect it to be material).
3) Approve priority postmortem + next-step remediation: alias rollout validation gate (INF-8421).

Naomi — please prepare a short customer note and SLA credit calc. Aditya — please coordinate the uplift and confirm when the revert goes live. Rishi — stand by for revert and full postmortem.

I will keep HealthRails execs on the thread and join the bridge.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: bridge-invite-20270721.txt)
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@healthrails.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@healthrails.com>, Jake Soto <jsoto@healthrails.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec summary: HealthRails 429 spike — ask for temporary uplift + credits

Monica / Redwood team —

Thanks for the quick triage and the uplift last night — we saw error rates return to baseline after the change. We appreciate the temporary throughput bump and the rapid revert.

We’d like a post-incident write-up that includes: timeline, root cause (alias/tiering mapping), mitigations applied, and steps to prevent recurrence. We’ll also share the support tickets that hit our SLAs so Naomi can correlate for credit calculation.

We accept the temporary uplift while we review the postmortem and will escalate internally if we spot residual anomalies. Please keep us updated when INF-8421 is scheduled for a deployment with the validation gate.

— Evan
Evan Cole
Head of Platform, HealthRails
